blocks.text: Nomenclature is the system of naming compounds. This section names alkanes (paraffins), their alkyl groups and cycloalkanes by the IUPAC rules, beginning with the alkane homologous series in 11.2.1, the rules for branched alkanes in 11.2.2 and cycloalkanes in 11.2.3.

blocks.prompt: Why does organic chemistry need a systematic (IUPAC) nomenclature?
blocks.explanation: The number of possible hydrocarbons grows enormously with the number of carbons, and many share a molecular formula. A systematic name built from the longest chain, the numbered positions and the substituents identifies one structure unambiguously, which common names such as isobutane cannot do for larger molecules.

items: IUPAC nomenclature names alkanes, alkyl groups and cycloalkanes systematically (11.2.1 to 11.2.3).
